quotes: We isolated genomic DNA from peripheral blood and surgically resected HH tissue in 55 patients with sporadic HH and intractable epilepsy.
Chromosomal abnormalities including the GLI3 locus were seen in 8 of 55 (15%) of the resected HH tissue samples. These somatic mutations appear to be highly variable.

records.label: Seven individuals from five families with bi-allelic SMO variants
quotes: we report bi-allelic loss-of-function variations in SMO in seven individuals from five independent families; these variations cause a wide phenotypic spectrum of developmental anomalies affecting the brain (hypothalamic hamartoma and microcephaly), heart (atrioventricular septal defect), skeleton (postaxial polydactyly, narrow chest, and shortening of long bones), and enteric nervous system (aganglionosis)

notes.statement: Le et al. (2020) found bi-allelic loss-of-function variants in the SMO gene in 7 individuals from 5 unrelated families with a wide range of developmental anomalies. These included hypothalamic hamartoma, microcephaly, atrioventricular septal defect, postaxial polydactyly, narrow chest, shortened long bones, and aganglionosis.
quotes: we report bi-allelic loss-of-function variations in SMO in seven individuals from five independent families

notes.statement: In cells from affected individuals, Le et al. (2020) found that ciliogenesis was normal but hedgehog signal transduction was severely altered. This resulted either from altered primary cilium trafficking or from abnormal activation of the pathway downstream of SMO. GLI2 accumulated at the cilium tip independently of hedgehog, suggesting that SMO may regulate basal ciliary trafficking of GLI2 when the pathway is off.
quotes: Cells derived from affected individuals showed normal ciliogenesis but severely altered Hh-signal transduction as a result of either altered PC trafficking or abnormal activation of the pathway downstream of SMO.
Hh-independent GLI2 accumulation at the PC tip in cells from the affected individuals suggests a potential function of SMO in regulating basal ciliary trafficking of GLI2 when the pathway is off.

notes.statement: Rubino et al. (2019) described endoscopic endonasal biopsy and subtotal resection of a large hypothalamic hamartoma in one of 2 brothers with a familial syndrome caused by germline SMO mutations.
quotes: The authors discuss the endoscopic endonasal biopsy and subtotal resection of a large hypothalamic hamartoma in one of the patients as well as the histopathological findings encountered.

notes.statement: Rubino et al. (2019) stated that theirs was the first familial syndrome associated with hypothalamic hamartomas other than Pallister-Hall syndrome, which is caused by truncation of GLI3.
quotes: the first familial syndrome associated with hypothalamic hamartomas other than Pallister-Hall syndrome

notes.statement: Craig et al. (2008) compared paired blood and resected tumor DNA from 55 patients with sporadic, nonsyndromic hypothalamic hamartoma (HH) and intractable epilepsy. Resequencing GLI3 found no causative germline mutations. They did find somatic chromosomal abnormalities including the GLI3 locus in 8 of the 55 (15%) HH tissue samples: a 7p copy-number abnormality in 1 sample and loss of heterozygosity within GLI3 in 8 samples (3 found by resequencing and 5 more by genotyping 28 SNPs).
quotes: we identified a somatic chromosomal abnormality on chromosome 7p in one HH tissue sample. Resequencing of GLI3 did not identify causative germline mutations but did identify LOH within the GLI3 gene in the HH tissue samples of three patients.
Further genotyping of 28 SNPs within and surrounding GLI3 identified five additional patients exhibiting LOH.
Chromosomal abnormalities including the GLI3 locus were seen in 8 of 55 (15%) of the resected HH tissue samples.

notes.statement: Craig et al. (2008) concluded that the development of chromosomal abnormalities within GLI3 is associated with the pathogenesis of HH lesions in sporadic, nonsyndromic patients. They noted that these somatic mutations appeared to be highly variable.
quotes: Together, these data provide evidence that the development of chromosomal abnormalities within GLI3 is associated with the pathogenesis of HH lesions in sporadic, nonsyndromic patients with HH and intractable epilepsy.
These somatic mutations appear to be highly variable.

notes.statement: Craig et al. (2008) noted that hypothalamic hamartomas are rare, benign congenital tumors associated with intractable epilepsy. Most cases are sporadic and nonsyndromic, and approximately 5% are associated with Pallister-Hall syndrome.
quotes: Hypothalamic hamartomas (HH) are rare, benign congenital tumors associated with intractable epilepsy. Most cases are sporadic and nonsyndromic. Approximately 5% of HH cases are associated with Pallister-Hall syndrome (PHS), which is caused by haploinsufficiency of GLI3.

notes.statement: Encha-Razavi et al. (1992) noted that, as far as they knew, isolated skeletal dysplasia with congenital hypothalamic hamartoma had not been reported before. In their analysis of reported Pallister-Hall syndrome cases, only skeletal dysplasia and oro-facial abnormalities were always present.
quotes: As far as we know, the association between isolated skeletal dysplasia and congenital hypothalamic hamartomas has not yet been documented in the literature.
A detailed analysis of the PHS reported cases shows that only skeletal dysplasia and oro-facial abnormalities are present constantly.

notes.statement: Encha-Razavi et al. (1992) proposed treating skeletal dysplasia and oro-facial abnormalities with hypothalamic hamartoma as the minimum criteria for a distinct, possibly familial entity, which they called 'congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome' (CHHS).
quotes: These findings prompt us to consider skeletal dysplasia and oro-facial abnormalities as common denominator and minimum criteria required to define a nosologically distinct, possibly familial entity, which we suggest calling "congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome" (CHHS).
